artifact_schema.description: One distinguished point of the shared walk with its coefficients: a*P + b*Q = (x, y), low DP_BITS bits of x zero, 2y <= p. Exactly these four keys.

x.description: x-coordinate, lowercase hex, no prefix, no leading zero; low DP_BITS bits zero

statement: Contribute distinguished points to the shared Pollard rho search for the 50-bit nothing-up-my-sleeve instance of GOAL-ecdlp-nums-50. This objective pays for the search; objective-nums-50.json pays for the answer. Run the walk in examples/certicom-ecdlp/jobs/nums-50-rho.json (job id bb124c668c79323b856c54372a720339895bcb4fd0599365bd7cf4706a4c855e; `tools/rho_dp.py walk --job ... --walker I` in pure Python, or `crypto cryptanalysis rho-collab work` in Rust). Each walker runs about 2^16 steps to a point whose low 16 bits of x are zero. Submit that point as exactly {"x", "y", "a", "b"} in lowercase hex with y canonical (2y <= p) and a*P + b*Q = (x, y). Each novel accepted point pays unit_price from the pool until the pool is empty; a point already paid mints nothing. Ask work_assignment for your unit range so contributors walk disjoint indices, but any valid point is paid whichever index it came from. Two artifacts for one point with different coefficients are a collision: `tools/rho_dp.py collide` computes k from them, and k settles objective-nums-50.json. About 640 points are expected before that happens.
